topics.label: Introduction to Cancer Evolution and Lecture Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: It frames the session by introducing the key themes of cancer evolution, microenvironmental interactions, and the intended learning outcomes.

topics.label: Genetic Clonal Selection and Epigenetic Drivers in Cancer Development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics demonstrate how tumor progression is driven at the cellular level through Darwinian clonal selection of mutations and altered epigenetic states.

topics.label: Cell of Origin and Hierarchical Stem Cell Models in Malignancy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics investigate how tissue stem cell hierarchies and cell-of-origin properties determine susceptibility to malignant transformation.

topics.label: Microenvironmental Signals, Inflammation, and Stromal Support in Tumorigenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how permissive microenvironments, inflammatory signaling, and stromal co-dependencies drive tumor outgrowth and invasive progression.

topics.label: Experimental and Computational Methods for Analyzing Tumor Heterogeneity
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic reviews modern genomic, transcriptomic, and spatial technologies used to map cancer evolution and cellular interactions.

topics.label: Integrative Evolutionary Model of Cancer Outgrowth
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides a comprehensive synthesis of how genetic mutations, cell lineage, epigenetic plasticity, and microenvironmental factors co-evolve to permit malignancy.

topics.label: Conclusion and Preview of Next Lecture
topics.groupedBecause: It provides the closing administrative wrap-up and previews the upcoming topic of cancer therapy.
